accepted.text: M1: Integration by parts is applied in the form $\frac{\pm\lambda}{x^2}\ln x \pm \int \mu \frac{1}{x^2}\cdot\frac{1}{x}$ or equivalent. A1: $-\int \frac{-1}{2x^2}\cdot\frac{1}{x}$ or equivalent. You can ignore the dx. dM1: Depends on the previous M1.

accepted.label: a
accepted.text: A1: $-\frac{1}{2x^2}\ln x+\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{1}{2x^2}\right)\{+c\}$ or $=-\frac{1}{2x^2}\ln x-\frac{1}{4x^2}\{+c\}$ or $\frac{x^{-2}}{-2}\ln x-\frac{x^{-2}}{4}\{+c\}$ or $\frac{-1-2\ln x}{4x^2}\{+c\}$ or equivalent. You can ignore subsequent working after a correct stated answer.

accepted.label: b
accepted.text: M1: Some evidence of applying limits of 2 and 1 to their part (a) answer and subtracts the correct way round.

1st B1: Their constant term must be equal to 3 for this mark. 2nd B1 (M1 on epen): Forming a correct identity. This can be implied by later working. M1 (A1 on epen): Attempts to find the value of either one of their B or their C from their identity. This can be achieved by either substituting values into their identity or comparing coefficients and solving the resulting equations simultaneously.
Note: You can imply the 2nd B1 from either $\frac{9x^2+20x-10}{(x+2)(3x-1)}\equiv\frac{A(x+2)(3x-1)+B(3x-1)+C(x+2)}{(x+2)(3x-1)}$ or $\frac{5x-4}{(x+2)(3x-1)}\equiv\frac{B(3x-1)+C(x+2)}{(x+2)(3x-1)}$

Alternative Method 1: Initially dividing by (x + 2): $\frac{9x^2+20x-10}{(x+2)(3x-1)}\equiv\frac{9x+2}{(3x-1)}-\frac{14}{(x+2)(3x-1)}\equiv 3+\frac{5}{(3x-1)}-\frac{14}{(x+2)(3x-1)}$ B1: their constant term $=3$. $-14\equiv B(3x-1)+C(x+2)$ B1: Forming a correct identity. $\Rightarrow B=2, C=-6$ M1: Attempts to find either one of their B or their C from their identity. So $3+\frac{5}{(3x-1)}+\frac{2}{(x+2)}-\frac{6}{(3x-1)}$ and $3+\frac{2}{(x+2)}-\frac{1}{(3x-1)}$ A1: Correct answer in partial fractions.

Alternative Method 2: Initially dividing by (3x - 1): $\frac{9x^2+20x-10}{(x+2)(3x-1)}\equiv\frac{3x+\frac{23}{3}}{(x+2)}-\frac{\frac{7}{3}}{(x+2)(3x-1)}\equiv 3+\frac{\frac{5}{3}}{(x+2)}-\frac{\frac{7}{3}}{(x+2)(3x-1)}$ B1: their constant term $=3$. $-\frac{7}{3}\equiv B(3x-1)+C(x+2)$ B1: Forming a correct identity. $\Rightarrow B=\frac{1}{3}, C=-1$ M1: Attempts to find either one of their B or their C from their identity. So $3+\frac{\frac{5}{3}}{(x+2)}+\frac{\frac{1}{3}}{(x+2)}-\frac{1}{(3x-1)}$ and $3+\frac{2}{(x+2)}-\frac{1}{(3x-1)}$ A1: Correct answer in partial fractions.

accepted.label: c
accepted.text: Alternative method for 2nd M1 and 3rd M1 mark: $\{2\}\int\frac{(u-1)^2}{u}.(u-1)\,\mathrm{d}u=\{2\}\int\frac{(u^2-2u+1)}{u}.(u-1)\,\mathrm{d}u=\{2\}\int\left(u-2+\frac{1}{u}\right).(u-1)\,\mathrm{d}u=\{2\}\int(u^2-...)\,\mathrm{d}u$ 2nd M1: An attempt to expand $(u-1)^2$, then divide the result by $u$ and then go on to multiply by $(u-1)$. $=\{2\}\int\left(u^2-2u+1-u+2-\frac{1}{u}\right)\mathrm{d}u=\{2\}\int\left(u^2-3u+3-\frac{1}{u}\right)\mathrm{d}u$ 3rd M1: to give three out of four of $\pm Au^2, \pm Bu, \pm C$ or $\pm\frac{D}{u}$

accepted.label: d
accepted.text: Alternative method: In Cartesian and applying u = 2 – 2x: $\mathrm{Area}(R)=\int(2^u-1)\{\mathrm{d}x\}$, where $u=2-2x$ $=\int_4^0(2^u-1)(-\frac{1}{2})\{\mathrm{d}u\}$ M0: Unless a candidate writes $\int(2^{2-2x}-1)\{\mathrm{d}x\}$ Then apply the "working parametrically" mark scheme.

accepted.label: d
accepted.text: Alternative method: For substitution $u=2^t$: $\mathrm{Area}(R)=\int(2^t-1).\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\mathrm{d}t$ M1: Complete substitution for both $y$ and $\mathrm{d}x$. where $u=2^t\Rightarrow\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}t}=2^t\ln 2\Rightarrow\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}t}=u\ln 2$. $x=-1\to t=4\to u=16$ and $x=1\to t=0\to u=1$ B1: Both correct limits in $t$ or both correct limits in $u$. So $\mathrm{area}(R)=-\frac{1}{2}\int\frac{u-1}{u\ln 2}\mathrm{d}u$ If not awarded above, you can award M1 for this integral. $=-\frac{1}{2}\int\frac{1}{\ln 2}-\frac{1}{u\ln 2}\mathrm{d}u=\left\{-\frac{1}{2}\right\}\left(\frac{u}{\ln 2}-\frac{\ln u}{\ln 2}\right)$ M1*: Either $2^t\to\frac{u}{\ln 2}$ or $(2^t-1)\to\frac{u}{\pm\alpha(\ln 2)}-\frac{\ln u}{\ln 2}$ or $(2^t-1)\to\pm\alpha(\ln 2)(u)-\frac{\ln u}{\ln 2}$ A1: $(2^t-1)\to\frac{u}{\ln 2}-\frac{\ln u}{\ln 2}$ $\left\{-\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{u}{\ln 2}-\frac{\ln u}{\ln 2}\right]_{16}^{1}\right\}=-\frac{1}{2}\left(\left(\frac{1}{\ln 2}\right)-\left(\frac{16}{\ln 2}-\frac{\ln 16}{\ln 2}\right)\right)$ dM1*: Depends on the previous method mark. Substitutes their changed limits in u and subtracts either way round. $=\frac{15}{2\ln 2}-\frac{\ln 16}{2\ln 2}$ or $\frac{15}{2\ln 2}-2$ A1: or equivalent.

accepted.label: b
accepted.text: Alternative Method 3 for part (b): $\int_{16}^{10}\frac{1}{3-\theta}\mathrm{d}\theta=\int_0^t\frac{1}{125}\mathrm{d}t$ $=\left[-\ln|3-\theta|\right]_{16}^{10}=\left[\frac{1}{125}t\right]_0^t$ M1A1: $\ln 13$ M1: Substitutes limit of $\theta=10$ correctly. $-\ln 7--\ln 13=\frac{1}{125}t$ M1: Uses correct algebra to rearrange their own equation into the form $\pm0.008t=\ln C-\ln D$, where C, D are positive numerical values. $t=77.3799...=77$ (nearest minute) A1: awrt 77.

accepted.label: b
accepted.text: Alternative Method 4 for part (b): $\{\theta=16\Rightarrow\}\ 16=A\mathrm{e}^{-0.008t}+3$, $\{\theta=10\Rightarrow\}\ 10=A\mathrm{e}^{-0.008t}+3$ M1*: Writes down a pair of equations in A and t, for $\theta=16$ and $\theta=10$ with either A unknown or A being a positive or negative value. A1: Two equations with an unknown A. $-0.008t=\ln\left(\frac{13}{A}\right)$ or $-0.008t=\ln\left(\frac{7}{A}\right)$ M1: Uses correct algebra to solve both of their equations leading to answers of the form $-0.008t=\ln k$, where k is a positive numerical value. $t_{(1)}=\frac{\ln\left(\frac{13}{A}\right)}{-0.008}$ and $t_{(2)}=\frac{\ln\left(\frac{7}{A}\right)}{-0.008}$, $t=t_{(1)}-t_{(2)}$ M1: Finds difference between the two times. (either way round). $\left\{t=\frac{\ln\left(\frac{7}{13}\right)}{(-0.008)}\right\}=77.3799...=77$ (nearest minute) A1: awrt 77. Correct solution only.
